To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the heat of combustion of an organic fluorine compound can be obtained with an accuracy of about 0.3 percent by rotating-bomb combustion calorimetry and (b) the heat of formation of an organometallic compound can be obtained by rotating-bomb solution calorimetry with an accuracy of 0.5 to 0.6 percent.

(a) the combustion of organic fluorine and chlorine compounds is accompanied by an appreciable heat release, (b) the combustion of organometallic and other carbon compounds that contain metals is accompanied by an even larger heat release, and (c) the heat release from the combustion of these compounds can be measured by rotating-bomb combustion calorimetry, with an uncertainty of 2 percent or better

(1) for organic compounds of fluorine, the heat of combustion is equal to the sum of the heats of combustion of the corresponding organic compounds that contain hydrogen instead of fluorine, and (2) for organometallic and other carbon compounds that contain metals, the heat of reaction of the metal with carbon is equal to the heat of reaction with oxygen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the thermochemical properties of organic fluorine and carbon compounds of transition metals, particularly the heat of combustion and heat of formation.

the development of rotating-bond calorimetry for the determination of heats of formation and heats of combustion of organic compounds that contain fluorine and carbon compounds of the metals, particularly those that contain metals in the higher oxidation states.
the development of methods for the determination of the heats of combustion of organic compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rotating-bomb method has been found suitable for combustion of organic fluorine and carbon compounds of the elements of Groups I, II, IIIA, and IVA.
the calorimetry of organic fluorine and organometallic and other carbon compounds containing metals is now feasible.

rotating-bomb calorimeters, when properly constructed, maintained, calibrated, operated, and used, can provide reliable and accurate data for the combustion of organic fluorine, organic sulphur, organic chlorine, and organic bromine compounds, and of organic compounds of metals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
rotating-bomb calorimeters have proved useful in the study of the thermochemistry of a large number of organic compounds that contain fluorine, and a few compounds of carbon and metals.
the techniques developed for rotating-bond combustion calorimetry have been applied to a wide range of organic fluorine and organometallic and other carbon compounds.
rotating-bomb calorimeters are now in general use for accurate combustion calorimetric measurements of organic fluorine and organometallic and other carbon compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to determine the heats of combustion of organic fluorine-containing compounds with a precision of 0.1% or better.
the techniques developed for rotating-bond calorimetry of organic chlorine, bromine or sulphur compounds are applicable to organic fluorine compounds.
the techniques developed for rotating-bond calorimetry of organometallic and other carbon compounds are not very different from those used for organic compounds.
